text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Scottish literary critic THOMAS CARLYLE was born in 1795. Two of his more famous quotes are : "You might prove anything with figures", and "A well-written life is almost as rare as a well-lived one".
Spanish dictator General FRANCISCO FRANCO was born in 1892. He ruled the country from 1939 until his death in 1975.
Canadian actress DEANNA DURBIN, who first found fame as a teenage star, was born in 1922.
US guitarist, bassist, singer and songwriter CHRIS HILLMAN, who was a founding member of the 'Byrds', was born in 1942.
US drummer and songwriter DENNIS WILSON, who was one of the 'Beach Boys', was born in 1944. DENNIS, who was the only real surfer among the group members, drowned in December 1983.
American actor JEFF BRIDGES, whose films included "The Last Picture Show" and "Thunderbolt and Lightfoot", was born in 1949.
** EVENTS **
1872 : The American brigantine "Marie Celeste" was found

adrift in the Atlantic. Her captain and crew had mysteriously disappeared. The ship was deserted and the lifeboat was missing. The cargo of 1,700 barrels of alcohol was untouched. The captain's table was set for a meal that was never eaten. The ship had set sail from New York on November 7 bound for Genoa. There was a crew of eight and the captain's wife and daughter. There were no clues to their fate.
1913 : Suffragette EMMELINE PANKHURST was arrested in
Plymouth on her return from the United States.
1918 : WOODROW WILSON sailed for France, to become the
first American President to visit a foreign country.
1921 : Silent screen star "FATTY" ARBUCKLE was found not

guilty of rape and manslaughter. The jury voted 10 to 2 in the actor's favour. The charge arose from the death of Hollywood starlet VIRGINIA CRABBE following a drinking party in ARBUCKLE's hotel room. She was raped at the party and before she died in hospital she accused ARBUCKLE.
1947 : TENNESSEE WILLIAM's play "A Streetcar Named
Desire" was premiered on Broadway, with MARLON BRANDO and JESSICA TANDY in the leading roles.
1957 : One of London's thickest fogs was blamed for a

rail tragedy which claimed the lives of 92 people. Two packed trains crashed under a bridge which then collapsed onto the wrecked carriages. Rescue workers tried to lift away 50 tons of concrete which entombed the passengers. A third train narrowly missed ploughing into the wreckage. The driver had slowed due to poor visibility.
1968 : The Texas oil troubleshooter "RED" ADAIR arrived
in Bass Strait to cap a gas leak on Esso-BHP's gas and oil platform off Lakes Entrance.
1974 : British composer BENJAMIN BRITTEN died. His
best-known works include "BILLY BUDD", "PETER GRIMES" and "DEATH IN VENICE".
1986 : RUPERT MURDOCH announced a 1,800 million dollar
take-over bid for The Herald and Weekly Times newspaper group.
